newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Portugal seen rejecting 10-yr bond bids.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Portugal seen rejecting 10-yr bond bids.

text.p: Portugal's Institute for Public Credit Management (IGCP) is likely to consider yields around seven percent too high and reject all bids at its offer of 25 billion escudos of 10-year bonds on Tuesday, analysts said.
The IGCP rejected all bids at its last auction on March 4 when the average yield sought was 6.9903 percent.

With banks set to bid at around seven percent again for the February 2007 fixed-rate bonds, analysts said that the IGCP was likely to take the same line. The results of Tuesday's auction are due around 1100 GMT.
The last time the IGCP sold 10-year paper was on February 14 when the average yield was 6.6993 percent.

The instability of the bond and currency markets due to worries about a possible delay in European monetary union together with the risk of a rate rise in the United States would push domestic banks into seeking high yields at the auction, analysts said.
The February 2007 closed at 6.88 percent on the illiquid secondary market on Monday.
